protocol.one_question_per_batch_justification: JevXForDecision.forward shares one question across the state batch, so a batch is a set of states asking the SAME question; the option count is therefore uniform and no padded option column is produced. --phase shared-state shows the m-question call agrees with the per-question calls to float32 re-association with identical argmax, so this protocol is the same computation as the genuine multi-question forward.
protocol.head_init: every arm starts from bitwise-identical head weights (torch.manual_seed(1234) before the wrapper is built)

questions.provenance_reason: deterministic rule: stars == 1. The brief calls this real; it is a threshold on a REAL dataset label, so it is recorded here as DERIVED-from-a-real-label, which is the distinction that matters.

extra.omitted_questions: No aspect-level questions on Yelp. Yelp/yelp_review_full ships exactly one label field (the star rating), carries no aspect annotation, and no aspect-labelled source is reachable from it. Hand-writing aspect labels would be annotating a benchmark by hand and calling it real, so they are OMITTED. The only further obtainable 'questions' are restatements of the same star label, which add no information and would inflate the multi-question appearance without content.
